entities.summary: Abel Jacob Herzberg was a Dutch Jewish lawyer and writer, whose parents were Russian Jews who had come to the Netherlands from Lithuania. Herzberg was trained as a lawyer and began a legal practice in Amsterdam, and became known as a legal scholar also. He was a Zionist from an early age, and around the time of the outbreak of World War II he attempted to emigrate with his family to Palestine. During the war he remained active in Jewish organizations until he was interned, with his wife, in Bergen-Belsen concentration camp, where his legal background and status as a legal scholar earned him a seat on a prisoners' court.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: As a lawyer and legal scholar in Bergen-Belsen concentration camp, Herzberg played a key role in organizing prisoner trials and advocating for prisoners' rights, potentially influencing the treatment of Jewish prisoners during WWII.
